liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancing In The Street** (3 reviews): Weir opens energetically as balloons pop; the reviewer says it was the last one until 1976; Reviewer finds Weir's singing on Dancing In The Street quite charming [10][14][20]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): The Other One into Me and My Uncle and back is called the show's highlight; Both Other One segments feature lots of spaced-out jamming [12][13]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): Garcia forgets some lyrics in this song [20]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 review): Reviewer wonders whether the break or extra beat in the intro was intentional [20]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): A sudden, out-of-nowhere Space leads into Black Peter, a one-of-a-kind transition according to the reviewer [13]
- **Big River** (1 review): Reviewer, citing Dead List, says this very hot Big River was the first the band ever played [12]
- **The Same Thing** (1 review): Reviewer defends it as a slinky, very good version, rejecting another reviewer's view of it as a low point [16]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): The Not Fade Away, Goin' Down The Road, Not Fade Away sandwich is called cosmic [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-12-31.142687.fm.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac1644** (recommended): FM broadcast; 34 songs; 198 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd1971-12-31.168858.fm.ksan.menke.miller.fixed.flac2496**: FM broadcast; 31 songs; 211 min [3]
- **gd71-12-31.fm.lanum.135.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 32 songs; 177 min; rated 4.23/5 by 52 [9]. Said about its sound: Radio station DJ chatter is audible at times throughout the broadcast recording; This copy seems to run fast with a chipmunk-like quality compared with the reviewer's decades-old tape [12][21]
- **gd1971-12-31.141329.fm.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: FM broadcast; 33 songs; 197 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Bill Graham [1]
- Donna Godchaux joins the band for the Casey Jones encore [1]
- Weir explained the organ and piano were out of tune with each other, causing repeated tuning breaks [3]
- Donna Jean Godchaux is noted as playing with the band for the first time [3]
- Reviewer names it their favorite show of 1971, after a turbulent year for the band [10]
- Reviewer thinks this is the best of the band's several Me and My Uncle sandwiches inside The Other One [13]
- Reviewer says the 1972 New Year's show is far more mind-blowing than this 1971 one [14]
- Reviewer calls it the best, tightest New Year's Eve show the band ever played [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-12-31.142687.fm.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick; source: Source: KSAN > FM Master reel > cassette > pcm ( Sony ESX HiFi l-750) - Provided by Tim Dalton; Transfer: pcm > Sony SL-10 > Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer… [1]. Also: Source is the FM broadcast from KSAN San Francisco [1]
- **gd1971-12-31.168858.fm.ksan.menke.miller.fixed.flac2496**: taped by Recording  by Bob Menke; transferred by Transfer by Bob Menke Mastering by Charlie Miller  September 21, 2024; source: FM (KSAN-FM) > Master Reel (Teac/3.75ips) [3]. Also: KSAN broadcast recording shared by Bob Menke; a Big River dropout was repaired and pitch confirmed by Joe B. Jones [3]
- **gd71-12-31.fm.lanum.135.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard - FM [9]
- **gd1971-12-31.141329.fm.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick; source: Source: KSAN > FM Master reel > cassette > pcm ( Sony ESX HiFil-750) - Provided by Tim Dalton; Transfer: pcm > Sony SL-10 > Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer… [2]
